claims.text: Large Language Models can be integrated into qualitative research methodologies to support traditional deductive coding.
Running recursive LLM analyses across 160 iterations allows researchers to record variation in model output analogous to evaluation by multiple human coders.

evidence.description: The authors proposed a methodology putting sample interview text and a codebook into an LLM to request evidence and code presence.
Sample texts were inputted 160 times to record output variation across iterations, with each iteration representing a distinct deductive coder.

methodologies.name: Recursive LLM-assisted Deductive Qualitative Coding
methodologies.description: Inputting sample interview texts and qualitative codebooks into an LLM across 160 iterations to evaluate coding consistency and compare outputs with traditional human coders.

limitations.text: There are current operational limitations when applying LLMs directly to qualitative research praxis.
